hook: A smooth, faceless black statue that moves only when nobody is looking may sound familiar, but this one has its own temperament. The file is short, and it helps to picture the containment room as you read, with its watchers placed so they can keep an eye on each other as well as the statue.
whyItMatters: SCP-650 is built entirely around the jump scare: its whole anomaly is the moment you turn around. By keeping the shock and dropping any violence, the report ends up with an object that is oddly playful yet still deeply unnerving to share a room with. It shows how much mood a single choice of motive can set in a very short file.
thingsToNotice:
The twist is that the statue is harmless. Tests that varied how long sight was broken found it never attacks; it only slips silently into place right behind someone in a menacing pose so they jump when they turn, and the Foundation openly declines to investigate why. That makes the strict three-watcher setup look less like a defense against injury than a defense against being startled.

With staff who stop flinching, it changes tactics, keeping its distance but lounging on a table, sitting in a chair, or once cowering in a corner as if afraid, and those observers still came away uneasy. The Euclid upgrade came when it crossed to the far side of the site and appeared behind a doctor in his own office, and his note, demanding containment regardless of budget because a face-to-face scare in a dim room costs years of life, is the payoff.
